evidence: Types fit the ask on the frozen bytes. Gates: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:20 and tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:20,29 are all type = "binary" (3 criteria), each with explicit 'Fails if ...' conditions. Functional: all 43 criteria in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml are type = "binary" (grep count 43/43) and are behaviour outcomes (typing, undo, find/replace, run, save, stale-save refusal, etc.); a wording scan found no degree-of-quality language being forced into a binary bar (the only hit, line 83 'clearly wider than the editor', is a setup instruction). Polish: 6 criteria, all binary (tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:20,29,38,47,56,65), matching the frozen template whose polish criteria are also binary; each states observable pass/fail conditions, e.g. line 68 'Fails if the page needs sideways scrolling, if any of those five areas cannot be reached, if controls overlap or are clipped so they cannot be read or pressed', and line 32 'Exact wording is free ... Fails if a main control has no readable name, or if any of the three actions ends with no visible textual feedback'. Visual (craft): all 3 criteria are type = "likert", points = 5 (tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:20-21, 36-37, 52-53), and every level 5,4,3,2,1,0 has a described anchor, e.g. lines 25-30: '5: clear and comfortable throughout, numbers aligned, caret and selection easy to see. / 4: one or two minor distractions. / 3: usable but several readability flaws, or the caret or the selection is hard to see. / 2: code is hard to read or numbers are misaligned. / 1: mostly unreadable or visibly corrupted text. / 0: no editor is shown.'; likewise lines 41-46 and 57-62. This is the same shape as the template visual judge.toml (likert, points = 5, anchors 5..0). tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:9 tells the judge 'Each criterion is scored from 0 to 5 using the anchors written in it. Those anchors take precedence over any generic 1 to 5 hint from the scoring tool.' No craft criterion is binary and no likert block lacks an anchor. Per the skill's known false positive, the internal annotation ('Likert we dont use in rewrdkit') is not a reason to flag the shipped likert visual dimension. Counterexample attempts: (a) a functionally correct but ugly app is not zeroed by a binary craft bar - it loses gradation only inside the likert visual dimension; (b) a conforming app with an unusual colour palette is not failed by a binary taste check, and visual/prompt.md:22 forbids penalising hue choice. Neither produced a defect. Notes (not defects): (1) the hosted run on the EARLIER candidate shows the tool normalising likert as (raw-1)/4 (reward-details.json: raw 5 -> value 1.0, raw 4 -> value 0.75), so the '1' and '0' anchors both yield no credit (or 0 depends on tool clamping, which I did not measure); the 0 anchor is inherited from the frozen template and tools/score.py is byte-identical to the template after LF normalisation, so this is template behaviour, not a task defect. (2) Middle anchors for workspace_layout and component_finish are terse ('4: a few small inconsistencies.') but each level is distinguishable by count/severity and comparable to the template's. (3) cw_narrow_width_usable and cw_controls_feedback_and_labels contain mild judgement words ('understandable', 'cannot be read or pressed') but are bounded by concrete fail conditions, so binary is appropriate. (4) No configured judge run exists for these bytes; the likert anchors' behaviour under the judge is measured only on the earlier candidate, where the editor_readability level-3 anchor text differed ('3: usable but several readability flaws.').
